title: Termwise Tor acyclicity computes derived tensor
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and B a commutative R-algebra. A bounded cochain complex Q^\bullet of R-modules means R-modules Q^n with differentials d^n:Q^n\to Q^{n+1}, d^{n+1}d^n=0, and Q^n=0 for all but finitely many n. Assume Tor_i^R(Q^n,B)=0 for every n and every i>0, where Tor is the usual projective-resolution Tor [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. Let Q^\bullet\otimes_R^L B denote the left-derived tensor product in the derived category of R-modules, and Q^\bullet\otimes_R B the ordinary total tensor complex. Then the canonical map Q^\bullet\otimes_R^L B\to Q^\bullet\otimes_R B is a quasi-isomorphism, and consequently H^i(Q^\bullet\otimes_R^L B)\cong H^i(Q^\bullet\otimes_R B) for every i.

source.place: Tag 08IB, lemma-compare-base-change: Tor-independent comparison of derived tensors

proof.text: Choose a,b for the support and d=(b-a).toNat. Then b <= a+d even if b<a, so Q is supported in [a,a+d]. Prove the comparison universally over such Q and every K-flat resolution by induction on the natural number d. For d=0 the complex is supported only in degree a and the one-term theorem [lem-pc-single-support-tor-acyclic-tensor] applies to the hypothesis at a.

For a successor width let T=sigma_{>=a+1}Q. Its support lies in [a+1,a+1+d]. Below a+1 its terms are zero, hence projective, and their positive Tor vanishes. In every remaining degree its term is canonically isomorphic to Q^n. Apply the left-derived tensor functor defining Tor [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules] to this isomorphism to transport vanishing. The induction hypothesis therefore gives the comparison for T for every K-flat resolution. The single complex Q^a[-a] has its comparison by [lem-pc-single-support-tor-acyclic-tensor], transporting the Tor hypothesis through its degree-a isomorphism. Apply [lem-pc-tensor-comparison-stupid-tail] to the two universally quantified comparisons to obtain the comparison for Q.
Apply the interval induction to the original bounds. Its quasi-isomorphism gives an IsIso homologyMap in each degree by the standard QuasiIso instance in Mathlib.

lean.statement: theorem quasiIso_tensor_of_termwise_tor_acyclic {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra R B] (Q : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (hbounded : ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (Q.X n)) (hTor : ∀ (n : ℤ) (i : ℕ), 0 < i → IsZero (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} R) i).obj (Q.X n)).obj (ModuleCat.of R B))) (P : CochainComplex.KFlat (ModuleCat.{u} R)) (f : P.obj ⟶ Q) (hf : QuasiIso f) : QuasiIso ((((tensoringRight (ModuleCat.{u} R)).obj (ModuleCat.of R B)).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map f) ∧ ∀ i : ℤ, IsIso (homologyMap ((((tensoringRight (ModuleCat.{u} R)).obj (ModuleCat.of R B)).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map f) i)
lean.note: The canonical map is stated on an arbitrary K-flat resolution P.obj → Q, using the source repository’s CochainComplex.KFlat. Its tensor with B is the derived-to-ordinary comparison, read as complexes of R-modules as in the statement. No additional property of Q, R, or B is assumed.
